name: Keycloak role adapter
purpose: The module that lifts Keycloak's role claim shape into the reduced Principal's `roles[]` array. Owns the read from either `resource_access.<clientId>.roles` (per-client roles) or `realm_access.roles` (realm-wide roles) per the realm record's `roleClaimShape` field. Does NOT remap Keycloak role strings into project-defined vocabulary; that is a project-level concern.
responsibilities: Read roles from the verified claim record at the path declared by `roleClaimShape`: `client-roles` reads from `resource_access.<clientId>.roles`; `realm-roles` reads from `realm_access.roles` (AC-11107-1).

Populate the reduced Principal's `roles[]` with the resulting string list, or an empty array when the path is absent (not a refusal - the project's authoriser above the Principal decides whether an empty roles set is acceptable) (AC-11107-2).
Refuse a claim record whose expected path is present but not an array of strings with `KEYCLOAK_ROLES_MALFORMED`; emit `keycloak.roles_refused` carrying realmSlug and reason class (AC-11107-3).

Never remap or transform Keycloak role strings; a project that maps them onto its own project-role vocabulary authors an `enrichPrincipal` hook the session-bridge invokes after the role adapter has populated the raw roles.
internalStructure: One factory function producing an adapt closure over the realmConfig record (for the record's `roleClaimShape` and `clientId`). The read is a plain object-path lookup; the shape checks are structural.

interfaces.name: realmConfig
interfaces.description: Same source TAC-1201 reads: the realm-config module.

interfaces.name: auditSink
interfaces.description: Structured-event sink; carries realmSlug and reasonClass only.

tradeoffs: Fixing the two claim paths and refusing to invent a third keeps the adapter's surface small and reflects Keycloak's own vocabulary; a realm operator that chooses a non-standard claim path is a project-level ADR conversation, not a mechanism extension. Not remapping role strings inside the adapter keeps the mechanism generic across every Keycloak deployment; project-specific role vocabulary lives on the enrichPrincipal hook where it belongs.
